items.prose: The correlogram of 500 days of a return series: the ACF has one bar outside the band, $-0.38$ at lag 1. The PACF bars at lags 1 to 4 are $-0.38$, $-0.17$, $-0.09$, $-0.05$.
items.question: Which model fits, and what sign does its coefficient have?

options.why: An AR(1) with negative $\phi$ has an ACF that alternates in sign and decays: $\rho_2 = \phi^2 > 0$ would show at lag 2.
The sign of $\rho_1 = \theta/(1 + \theta^2)$ is the sign of $\theta$. A negative spike needs a negative $\theta$.

feedback.correct: Correct. One negative spike, a tailing PACF: MA(1), $\theta < 0$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which panel cuts off, and what sign is the spike?

explain.text: The ACF cuts off after lag 1, so it is an MA(1), and $\rho_1 < 0$ means $\theta < 0$. Solving $\theta/(1 + \theta^2) = -0.38$ gives $\theta \approx -0.47$. Bid-ask bounce in trade prices produces exactly this pattern.

items.prose: An MA(1) has a lag-1 autocorrelation of 0.4.
items.question: What is its invertible $\theta$?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Solve $0.4\theta^2 - \theta + 0.4 = 0$ and keep the root inside $[-1, 1]$.

byKey.rho: You set $\theta = \rho_1$. That is the AR rule; for an MA(1) $\rho_1 = \theta/(1 + \theta^2)$.
byKey.big: That root gives the same ACF but is not invertible. Keep $|\theta| < 1$.

explain.text: The roots are 0.5 and 2; their product is 1. We keep 0.5 so that the shocks can be recovered from past values.

items.prose: An ARMA(2, 1) with a constant is fitted to 800 days and reaches a maximised log-likelihood of $\ell = -1200.5$.
items.question: What is its AIC?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Count every estimated parameter, then compute $2k - 2\ell$.

byKey.k3: You counted the AR and MA terms only. The constant and $\sigma^2$ are estimated too.
byKey.k4: You left out one of the constant or $\sigma^2$.
byKey.sign: You added $2\ell$. AIC is $2k - 2\ell$, and $\ell$ is negative.

explain.text: $2k - 2\ell = 10 + 2401 = 2411$. AIC compares models fitted to the same data; the number alone means nothing.

items.prose: Four candidates, fitted to the same 600 days.
items.question: Which model do you choose?

options.why: You took the minimum at face value. ARMA(1, 0) is within 1.8 points, a tie by the rule of thumb, with two fewer parameters.

options.text: ARMA(1, 1): the middle of the tie
options.why: It ties, but it is not the smallest of the tied models. ARMA(1, 0) is.

feedback.correct: Correct. Within 2 AIC points, take the fewest parameters.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the models within 2 of the best, then the smallest.

explain.text: The best is 810.6. ARMA(1, 0) at 812.4 and ARMA(1, 1) at 811.2 are within 2; ARMA(2, 2) at 813.9 is not. The smallest tied model is ARMA(1, 0); check its residuals before you use it.

items.prose: An AR(1) has $\phi = 0.5$ and shock variance $\sigma^2 = 1$.
items.question: What is the 95% half-width of the 2-day forecast?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the variances of the two unknown shocks, the older one damped by $\phi$.

byKey.rw: You gave both shocks full weight, as for a walk.
byKey.sds: You added standard deviations, $1.96(1 + 0.5)$. Add variances.

explain.text: $Var(e_2) = \sigma^2(1 + \phi^2) = 1.25$, so the half-width is $1.96 \times 1.118 = 2.191$. The limit is $1.96/\sqrt{0.75} = 2.263$.

items.prose: An AR(1) has mean $\mu = 2$ and $\phi = 0.6$. Today $x_n = 5$.
items.question: What is the 3-day forecast?

feedback.correct: Correct. The gap of 3 shrinks to $0.216 \times 3$.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Shrink the gap from the mean by $\phi^3$, then add the mean.

byKey.zero: You shrank $x_n$ towards 0: $0.6^3 \times 5$. It shrinks towards the mean.
byKey.lin: That is the mean, the forecast far ahead.

items.prose: A spread follows an AR(1) with $\phi = 0.7$.
items.question: What is its half-life in days?

byKey.lin: You took 30% of the starting gap off each day. The decay is geometric.
byKey.flip: You divided the other way round.

items.prose: The regression $\Delta x_t = a + b\,x_{t-1}$ gives $b = -0.020$ with standard error 0.006, so $\hat\phi = 0.98$ and a half-life of 34.3 days.
items.question: What half-life does the upper end of the 95% interval for $b$ give?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add $1.96 \times 0.006$ to $b$, then map $\phi = 1 + b$ to days.

byKey.sym: You assumed the interval is symmetric about 34.3. The map from $\phi$ to days is steep near 1.
byKey.lo: That is the lower end, from $b - 1.96\,\text{se}$.

explain.text: $b$ runs from $-0.0318$ to $-0.0082$, so $\phi$ from 0.968 to 0.992 and the half-life from 21.5 to 83.8 days. The estimate of 34 days is the least uncertain-looking part of a very uncertain answer.
